title: How ScanFinder learns to file by itself
description: Explains auto-file and graduation: the Home 'Getting smarter' card, then Settings → Processing where the graduation count and confidence threshold live. The arc (teach once → confirm a few clean → the sender graduates → its documents file themselves) is narrated over the real controls, with the reassurance that anything unsure still waits in Review. No graduated supplier is faked.

steps.narration: As ScanFinder learns your suppliers, it starts filing their documents for you, with no review needed at all. Here's how that happens — and why you can trust it.
steps.caption: How it learns to file by itself

steps.narration: The dashboard keeps score here. It shows how many of your suppliers ScanFinder can now file on its own, and how many document layouts it has learned so far.
steps.caption: The dashboard tracks what it has learned

steps.narration: The path to that is simple. You teach a supplier once, then confirm its first few documents in Review. Every clean confirmation — where you didn't have to change a thing — builds ScanFinder's confidence in that sender.
steps.caption: Teach once, then confirm a few clean ones

steps.narration: You set the details in Settings.
steps.caption: 1. Open Settings

steps.narration: This is the important one. It's how many clean confirmations a sender needs before ScanFinder trusts it — five by default. Once a supplier passes that mark it graduates, and from then on its documents file themselves the moment they're read.
steps.caption: Confirmations before a sender is trusted

steps.narration: This sets how sure it must be before filing anything on its own. It's kept deliberately high and cautious to begin with; as the reads on your regular suppliers settle, you can ease it down a little to let more through.
steps.caption: How sure it must be to file automatically

steps.narration: Automatic filing is switched on here, and there's a firm rule behind it: it only ever files a document that read cleanly, with nothing at all flagged for a look.
steps.caption: Auto-file is on — clean reads only

steps.narration: That's the safety net. If ScanFinder is ever unsure — a supplier it hasn't met, or a date it couldn't read clearly — it never guesses. It sets that one document aside in Review for you. So the more you use it, the less it asks — and it will never file something it isn't certain about.
steps.caption: Unsure? It always waits in Review

steps.narration: Teach your regular senders, confirm the first few, and your filing quietly starts running itself.
steps.caption: Teach · confirm a few · then hands-off
